feature_representation_caveat: The models share the same data split and source data, but the representation is model-appropriate rather than identical: SVM/Random Forest/XGBoost use the project's TF-IDF word/char n-grams + count vectorizer + 23 deterministic CWE-89/CWE-295 security features (ml/feature_pipeline.py, unchanged), while LSTM uses a learned embedding over a code-aware token sequence (research_eval/lstm_train.py's tokenizer). This is a real architectural difference, not an oversight - input representations are NOT identical.
note: Ranks are 1=best. No claim of 'LSTM is better' is made unless the table itself supports it.
